title: SLO alignment + cost-velocity canvas
content:
Purpose
This working canvas ties launch-readiness decisions to concrete SLOs and the expected cost/velocity tradeoffs across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Who this is for
- Product Ops / Product Managers: choose acceptable KPI thresholds for go/no-go and phase gates.
- Platform/Serving teams: understand SLO targets to tune autoscale/batching.
- Solutions/SEs: articulate customer tradeoffs (latency vs unit cost) during pilots.

High-level thesis
We treat SLOs as levers for traffic phasing: stricter latency/availability SLOs push customers to Dedicated or higher-cost model variants, while relaxed SLOs allow cost-optimized paths (larger batch windows, quantized models). This doc maps those levers to measurable KPIs and ops actions.

Key definitions (operational)
- Availability SLO: % of requests returned with 2xx within 99th percentile window (defined per route). Example target: 99.95% for core UI endpoints.
- Latency SLO: p95/p99 end-to-end generation time (time-to-first-token for streaming routes).
- Quality guardrail: prompt-set pass rate (automated evals on canary prompts) — % of prompts that meet quality threshold.
- Unit cost signal: $/1k prompt-tokens (includes compute + infra overhead).
- Traffic velocity: requests/minute for the route, used for capacity gating.

KPI mapping canvas (text table)
Columns: KPI | Launch gate (internal) | Pilot phase target | Scale target | Measurement method | Owner
- Availability | emergency-gate | 99.9% | 99.95% | infra tracing + synthetic probes | infra-sre (Jordan)
- Latency (p95) | performance-gate | 450ms | 300ms | synthetic & sampled real traffic | serving-runtime (Ravi)
- Cost per 1k tokens | cost-gate | $3.80 | $2.25 | billing pipeline, token buckets | product-ops (Maya)
- Quality pass rate | quality-gate | 92% | 97% | auto-evals + hand-labeled spot-checks | applied-ml (Elena)
- Time to rollback | safety-gate | <5m | <2m | incident playbook logs | product-ops / srep

Notes on cost metric: we use $/1k prompt-tokens as a normalized currency across routes and model families. For dedicated deployments we show both amortized committed cost and burst delta — display both in ops dashboards.

Readiness checklist (pre-launch to 100k daily requests)
Core preflight (must be green before enabling public beta):
- [ ] Canary traffic run: 24h steady load at expected pilot velocity (owner: serving-runtime)
- [ ] Synthetic quality sweep: 500 canonical prompts across top 10 intents (owner: applied-ml)
- [ ] Cost smoke: run 10k requests with production batching settings to validate $/1k estimate (owner: product-ops)
- [ ] Fallback routing validated: model-variant fallback works for 429s/timeout (owner: infra)
- [ ] Observability: per-route token cost, p95/p99, error-rate charting added to launch dashboard (owner: observability)

Phase gating (phases + trigger signals)
- Phase 0 (internal alpha, dev testers): feature flags only. Triggers to move to Phase 1: quality pass >= 90% on seed prompts, no latency p95 > 800ms incidents in 48h.
- Phase 1 (closed beta, 1–10k DAU): open to pilot customers. Triggers to move to Phase 2: cost per 1k tokens within 10% of target, availability >= 99.9% over 7d rolling.
- Phase 2 (public beta, 10–100k DAU): expand cohort. Triggers to move to Phase 3: sustained throughput within autoscale headroom, quality pass >= 95%.
- Phase 3 (general availability): final commercial SLA; legal/contract signoffs, audit logging validated.

Operational playbook snippets
- If p95 latency exceeds target for 10m sustained: immediately shift non-critical traffic to lower-cost model variant and enable prefix-caching for the top 5 intents. Run a rolling restart of worker pool with adjusted batch window. (Owner: serving-runtime / oncall)
- If quality pass rate drops >4 percentage points vs baseline: pause rollout, demote to previous model version, create a regression ticket for model-onboarding team, notify affected pilot customers. (Owner: applied-ml + SE)
- Cost overrun alert (unit cost > target +15% for 1h): switch routing to burst pool (if available), enable tighter batching, and open a cost-ops war room to assess traffic and billing delta. (Owner: product-ops)

Owner roster and escalation contacts
- Product Ops (Maya Thompson) — kpi owner, gate decision authority for pilot -> beta
- Serving Runtime (Ravi Patel) — latency and autoscale adjustments
- Applied ML (Elena Gomez) — quality guardrails and prompt-set maintenance
- Infra / SRE (Jordan Blake) — availability, fallback routing, rollbacks
- Solutions Eng (TBD) — customer communication during gating

Short ramp plan (milestones & sample sprint tasks)
Week -4 (prep): finalize canary prompts, baseline metrics capture, billing sandbox run
Week -2 (canary): 24h canary @ pilot velocity; collect p95/p99, quality, cost
Week 0 (pilot launch): onboard 3 pilot customers, monitor 48h; daily standups with ops leads
Week 2 (pilot review): decide phase gating; either widen beta cohort or rollback
Week 6 (public beta): open to broader customers if gating satisfied

Decision rubric (simple)
- Proceed if all gate KPIs are within pilot targets AND no unresolved critical incidents older than 24h.
- Hold if unit cost > pilot target by >20% OR quality pass < pilot target.
- Rollback immediately if availability < 99% or p99 latency > 2x target for >30m.

Open questions / next steps (notes to self)
- Need a standard way to compute amortized per-route committed cost for Dedicated customers — estimate model fit vs committed GPU types. (action: cost-modeling deep-dive)
- Add a synthetic prompt variant generator so we stress rare intents that might trigger long-tail latency. (action: applied-ml)
- Validate handoff checklist for SEs to communicate degraded quality scenarios to pilot customers. (action: solutions-eng)

Appendix: quick-template for launch card (copy into tickets)
- Route name / endpoint: 
- Pilot cohort: 
- Pilot velocity target (req/min): 
- Pilot KPIs (availability / p95 / quality / $/1k): 
- Canary dates: 
- Rollout owner + oncall contact: 
- Go/hold/rollback criteria summary: 

End of canvas — treat this as a living doc. Update owners and numeric targets after each pilot review.
